label: Riverside
rationale: Rollins's last Riverside album and his most overtly ambitious 1950s statement: the 19-minute title suite is an extended through-composed trio performance with Oscar Pettiford and Max Roach, recorded while Rollins was framing his music as a civil-rights statement (his original liner note was famously toned down by the label). A piano-less trio record at the peak of the Way Out West / Village Vanguard period, with Roach in devastating form — consensus praise across AllMusic (4.5 stars, Yanow: 'a near masterpiece'), Penguin Guide (3.5 stars), and the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide (5 stars). Session gravity is exceptional: Pettiford and Roach are two of the defining rhythm players of the era, and this is one of the great documents of all three.

cover_art.notes: Front image from a release in the correct MusicBrainz release group; pressing not verified as original Riverside RLP 12-258.

personnel_record.notes: Riverside RLP 12-258. Session distribution per Wikipedia (citing jazzdisco.org Rollins catalog): February 11, 1958 = tracks 2-5; March 7, 1958 = track 1 ('The Freedom Suite'). A CD-reissue alternate take of 'Till There Was You' (4:55) is excluded as a bonus track. AllMusic gives recording location only as 'New York, NY'; Wikipedia gives WOR Recording Studio for both dates — consistent (WOR ⊂ NYC). Producers Orrin Keepnews and Bill Grauer per both Wikipedia and AllMusic credits (AllMusic lists 'Bill Grauer, Jr.'); engineer Sam Morse per AllMusic credits. Paul Bacon (design), Paul Weller (photography) also credited by AllMusic.

ballot.case_for: A consensus-backed landmark at the canon's center of gravity: AllMusic 4.5 stars (Yanow: 'a near masterpiece'), Penguin Guide 3.5, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 5 stars. It is a defining statement of the piano-less trio format Rollins pioneered — the 19-minute through-composed title suite was a structural leap for a 1958 hard-bop record — and one of the earliest explicit civil-rights statements in the post-bebop LP era, predating Roach's own We Insist! Session gravity is exceptional: Rollins at his Way Out West / Village Vanguard peak with Oscar Pettiford and Max Roach, two of the era's defining rhythm players, makes this one of the great documents of all three.
ballot.case_against: The album is structurally lopsided: the monumental 19-minute original suite occupies Side A while Side B is four standard show tunes, making it arguably a less complete top-to-bottom statement than the era's uniform masterpieces. The extended piano-less title track also demands real stamina from a cold listener, slightly lowering its pure discovery-test score for a novice. Sourcing is adequate but not bulletproof — the dossier leans on Wikipedia and AllMusic, with session-date mapping resting on Wikipedia's citation of jazzdisco.org rather than a directly consulted primary discography.
ballot.disagreement: No substantive disagreement: Reference 1 (deepseek-v4-pro) returned an empty response, so only Reference 2 (gemini-3.1-pro-preview) argued the case. That single reference landed consensus_core/strong, and the for-case aligns with the dossier's own evidence; the tier is set accordingly but on one voice rather than two.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John treat Freedom Suite as consensus_core at strong priority — an elite-personnel, civil-rights-era Rollins landmark whose against-case (side imbalance, discovery friction, adequate-but-thin sourcing) does not rise to the level of a contest.
